articles.headline: No. 3 Louisville women use 26-0 run to ease past Alaska Anchorage 113-40 in Great Alaska Shootout
articles.description: — Elif Istanbulluoglu scored 19 points, Imari Berry had 13 of her 16 in the first quarter, and No. 3 Louisville used a big third-quarter run to ease past Alaska Anchorage 113-40 on Saturday night in the Great Alaska Shootout.

articles.headline: NCAA to scrap pregame handshakes at women's tourney after Auriemma-Staley spat
articles.description: The NCAA will encourage but no longer mandate pregame handshakes between head coaches at the women's tournament after last season's controversy involving Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley.

articles.headline: Iowa State to begin 'enhanced monitoring' of Bill Fennelly, women's hoops team
articles.description: Iowa State addressed recent allegations of "verbal" and "emotional" abuse against head coach Bill Fennelly and said it will institute "enhanced monitoring" of the women's basketball team.

articles.headline: Harpring scores 20, No. 24 North Carolina women pull away from Alabama
articles.description: — Kate Harpring scored 20 points, Achol Akot added 16 and No. 24 North Carolina used two runs in the second half on Saturday to defeat Alabama 78-64 at the WBCA Showcase.

article.headline: Grocholski scores 25 points, grabs 11 rebounds, No. 17 Minnesota women top Marquette 87-79
article.description: — Grace Grocholski hit five 3-pointers and scored 25 points with 11 rebounds; Leah Harmon drained a clutch 3-pointer, and No. 17 Minnesota turned back Marquette 87-79 on Saturday.

article.story: MILWAUKEE -- — Grace Grocholski hit five 3-pointers and scored 25 points with 11 rebounds; Leah Harmon drained a clutch 3-pointer, and No. 17 Minnesota turned back Marquette 87-79 on Saturday. Grocholski's 7-0 run put the Golden Gophers (2-0) on top 60-46 late in the third quarter, and the lead stayed in double figures until less than three minutes remained. The Golden Eagles (1-1) got within 78-73 on a layup by Mackenzie Givens with 1:42 to go, but Harmon answered that with a 3. From there, the Gophers went 6 of 6 from the foul line. Harmon finished with 17 points, Natalie Kussow and reserve Tori Oehrlein both had 12 and Mara Braun 11. Halle Vice led Marquette with 25 points on 11-of-14 shooting. You Han Lin had 14 points off the bench, Kayl Petersen had 12 and Givens added 10. The Golden Eagles shot 58% (32 of 55) with nine 3-pointers, but Minnesota used 21 offensive rebounds to score 21 second-chance points and turned 17 turnovers into 23 points. Grocholski was 4-of-4 shooting behind the arc and had 14 points as the Gophers took a 41-33 lead at the break. Minnesota opened the game with 12 points, starting with 3-pointers from Braun and Grocholski, but quickly cooled off, and the Golden Eagles were within 20-19 at the end of the first quarter. With the first two buckets of the second quarter, Marquette took its only lead. Minnesota responded with a 19-5 run to get the lead to 39-29. Marquette had 11 turnovers that cost 17 points. Up next Minnesota: Home against Southern on Tuesday.
